L0101.text: Everything in this harbour is made up, except the kind of room in that window.
L0101.spoken: Everything in this harbour is made up, except the kind of room in that window.

L0102.text: It is a chat room, the very example Durable Objects began with, in 2020.
L0102.spoken: It is a chat room, the very example Durable Objects began with, in 2020.

L0103.text: Someone types message forty-two: the ferry is late.
L0103.spoken: Someone types message forty-two: the ferry is late.

L0104.text: It waits at the door. Then it gets its tick: a promise that it is saved.
L0104.spoken: It waits at the door. Then it gets its tick: a promise that it is saved.

L0105.text: Then House A goes dark, and the square goes quiet.
L0105.spoken: Then House A goes dark, and the square goes quiet.

L0106.text: Up the hill, House C lights. Its keeper, the runtime, draws a bundle from the well, and the room relights in a new window.
L0106.spoken: Up the hill, House C lights. Its keeper, the runtime, draws a bundle from the well, and the room relights in a new window.

L0107.text: Message forty-two is still there, with its tick.
L0107.spoken: Message forty-two is still there, with its tick.

L0108.text: The machine that made that promise is gone. The promise is still true.
L0108.spoken: The machine that made that promise is gone. The promise is still true.

L0109.text: How did the promise outlive the machine?
L0109.spoken: How did the promise outlive the machine?

L0110.text: The answer is in the square: the town well, which is a storage bucket.
L0110.spoken: The answer is in the square: the town well, which is a storage bucket.

L0111.text: The plate above it names the room's owner.
L0111.spoken: The plate above it names the room's owner.

L0112.text: The room keeps two promises: one owner at a time, and nothing acknowledged is lost when a machine fails.
L0112.spoken: The room keeps two promises: one owner at a time, and nothing acknowledged is lost when a machine fails.

L0113.text: And a newer one, still being built: the room can move between machines you run.
L0113.spoken: And a newer one, still being built: the room can move between machines you run.

L0114.text: So how can a bucket, which cannot run a single line of code, make a room portable?
L0114.spoken: So how can a bucket, which cannot run a single line of code, make a room portable?

L0115.text: A story from 2020 to the end of October 2026: a room, a well and a ribbon.
L0115.spoken: A story from 2020 to the end of October 2026: a room, a well and a ribbon.

L0116.text: The harbour is ours. The machinery is real code, and every piece wears a tag saying whose.
L0116.spoken: The harbour is ours. The machinery is real code, and every piece wears a tag saying whose.

L0117.text: The newest of it is days old, and still experimental.
L0117.spoken: The newest of it is days old, and still experimental.

L0201.text: On the twenty-eighth of September, 2020, Kenton Varda of Cloudflare introduced Durable Objects, in a closed beta.
L0201.spoken: On the twenty-eighth of September, 2020, Kenton Varda of Cloudflare introduced Durable Objects, in a closed beta.

L0202.text: Each object has an identifier that is unique across the whole world.
L0202.spoken: Each object has an identifier that is unique across the whole world.

L0203.text: And his post is plain about where that object lives.
L0203.spoken: And his post is plain about where that object lives.

L0204.text: In one place. Only ever one, at a time.
L0204.spoken: In one place. Only ever one, at a time.

L0205.text: So every request about the same thing reaches the same place, and that place can coordinate them.
L0205.spoken: So every request about the same thing reaches the same place, and that place can coordinate them.

L0207.text: His demonstration is a chat app: each chat room is one object, and every message passes through it to everyone else.
L0207.spoken: His demonstration is a chat app: each chat room is one object, and every message passes through it to everyone else.

L0208.text: That is the kind of room our lantern holds: one room, one object, one home.
L0208.spoken: That is the kind of room our lantern holds: one room, one object, one home.

L0209.text: Notice what one home does not mean. A handler can stop and wait, and living in one place does not make all its steps one transaction.
L0209.spoken: Notice what one home does not mean. A handler can stop and wait, and living in one place does not make all its steps one transaction.

L0210.text: The third of August, 2021. A later post of his is called Easy, Fast, Correct: Choose three.
L0210.spoken: The third of August, 2021. A later post of his is called Easy, Fast, Correct: Choose three.

L0211.text: It puts a gate on the room's door, an output gate. While a write is unfinished, the reply to our sender waits behind a latch.
L0211.spoken: It puts a gate on the room's door, an output gate. While a write is unfinished, the reply to our sender waits behind a latch.

L0212.text: The write completes. The latch lifts, and the letter goes out.
L0212.spoken: The write completes. The latch lifts, and the letter goes out.

L0213.text: If the write fails, the waiting letters are thrown away, replaced with errors, and the object restarts.
L0213.spoken: If the write fails, the waiting letters are thrown away, replaced with errors, and the object restarts.

L0214.text: So the tick in the harbour was a held letter, released.
L0214.spoken: So the tick in the harbour was a held letter, released.

L0215.text: September 2022. Cloudflare opens the source of its runtime, workerd.
L0215.spoken: September 2022. Cloudflare opens the source of its runtime, worker D.

L0216.text: Now the runtime could leave Cloudflare, and a room could come too, but only as a single instance on one machine. In 2026 Ryan Dahl would call it exactly that: limited to a single instance.
L0216.spoken: Now the runtime could leave Cloudflare, and a room could come too, but only as a single instance on one machine. In 2026 Ryan Dahl would call it exactly that: limited to a single instance.

L0217.text: September 2024. SQLite moves inside the object, into the very same thread as its code.
L0217.spoken: September 2024. S Q L lite moves inside the object, into the very same thread as its code.

L0219.text: But a tick is not a local read. A tick says the write will outlive the machine.
L0219.spoken: But a tick is not a local read. A tick says the write will outlive the machine.

L0220.text: On Cloudflare's own network, a hosted service kept that promise: the Storage Relay Service.
L0220.spoken: On Cloudflare's own network, a hosted service kept that promise: the Storage Relay Service.

L0221.text: It watches SQLite's write-ahead log, where each change is written first, and ships the changes to object storage in batches: ten seconds, or sixteen megabytes, at the most.
L0221.spoken: It watches S Q L lite's write-ahead log, where each change is written first, and ships the changes to object storage in batches: ten seconds, or sixteen megabytes, at the most.

L0222.text: Object storage is slow, and nobody can wait ten seconds for a tick.
L0222.spoken: Object storage is slow, and nobody can wait ten seconds for a tick.

L0223.text: So each commit also goes straight to five followers, in five different data centres. When three answer, the latch lifts.
L0223.spoken: So each commit also goes straight to five followers, in five different data centres. When three answer, the latch lifts.

L0224.text: Real machinery. And all of it lived inside Cloudflare.
L0224.spoken: Real machinery. And all of it lived inside Cloudflare.

L0301.text: Back to the square. In our harbour the Well stands for a bucket in an object store, like Amazon's S3.
L0301.spoken: Back to the square. In our harbour the Well stands for a bucket in an object store, like Amazon's S three.

L0302.text: There was a time when overwriting a file in S3 and reading it straight back could hand you the old copy.
L0302.spoken: There was a time when overwriting a file in S three and reading it straight back could hand you the old copy.

L0303.text: Amazon later explained why: a write could take one path through its caches, and a read another.
L0303.spoken: Amazon later explained why: a write could take one path through its caches, and a read another.

L0304.text: On the first of December, 2020, that changed: read after a write, and you get the latest.
L0304.spoken: On the first of December, 2020, that changed: read after a write, and you get the latest.

L0305.text: Whatever bucket you draw up is the newest.
L0305.spoken: Whatever bucket you draw up is the newest.

L0306.text: The job: the room's Plate is empty, and Houses A and B both want it.
L0306.spoken: The job: the room's Plate is empty, and Houses A and B both want it.

L0307.text: Fresh reads are not enough. Pull the pin from the Well's brass tooth, and the Well checks nothing.
L0307.spoken: Fresh reads are not enough. Pull the pin from the Well's brass tooth, and the Well checks nothing.

L0308.text: Each keeper reads the Plate: nobody. Each writes: mine.
L0308.spoken: Each keeper reads the Plate: nobody. Each writes: mine.

L0309.text: Both lanterns light; both rooms take messages.
L0309.spoken: Both lanterns light; both rooms take messages.

L0310.text: B's plate lands a moment later and wins the Well. But A has already answered its senders.
L0310.spoken: B's plate lands a moment later and wins the Well. But A has already answered its senders.

L0311.text: An overwrite can win the well. It cannot take back what was already served.
L0311.spoken: An overwrite can win the well. It cannot take back what was already served.

L0312.text: Between the read and the write, the world moved. Pin back.
L0312.spoken: Between the read and the write, the world moved. Pin back.

L0313.text: The twentieth of August, 2024. S3 learns its first refusal: write this only if nothing is there.
L0313.spoken: The twentieth of August, 2024. S three learns its first refusal: write this only if nothing is there.

L0314.text: Two keepers race. One creation lands, a shutter drops, and the second card is refused.
L0314.spoken: Two keepers race. One creation lands, a shutter drops, and the second card is refused.

L0315.text: The twenty-fifth of November, 2024: replace this only if it is still the version I read.
L0315.spoken: The twenty-fifth of November, 2024: replace this only if it is still the version I read.

L0316.text: Both cards carry the same old version. One click: accepted, and the Plate's notch is cut anew. One thunk: refused.
L0316.spoken: Both cards carry the same old version. One click: accepted, and the Plate's notch is cut anew. One thunk: refused.

L0317.text: That is compare and swap, and the store checks the condition, not the keeper.
L0317.spoken: That is compare and swap, and the store checks the condition, not the keeper.

L0318.text: The Well had learned to say no.
L0318.spoken: The Well had learned to say no.

L0320.text: In April 2021, Werner Vogels, Amazon's chief technology officer, described what they had built inside S3.
L0320.spoken: In April 2021, Werner Vohgels, Amazon's chief technology officer, described what they had built inside S three.

L0321.text: Caches that agree with one another, an order for every object's changes, and a witness, told of every change, that any cache can ask: is my copy stale?
L0321.spoken: Caches that agree with one another, an order for every object's changes, and a witness, told of every change, that any cache can ask: is my copy stale?

L0322.text: They checked it with proofs and model checking, which, he wrote, was more work than building it.
L0322.spoken: They checked it with proofs and model checking, which, he wrote, was more work than building it.

L0323.text: So the houses on the hill run no consensus of their own. The coordination has moved inside the Well.
L0323.spoken: So the houses on the hill run no consensus of their own. The coordination has moved inside the Well.

L0324.text: Now a warning, from celld's own documentation.
L0324.spoken: Now a warning, from cell D's own documentation.

L0325.text: Some stores speak S3's language but do not keep these conditions; on them, two houses can own one room.
L0325.spoken: Some stores speak S three's language but do not keep these conditions; on them, two houses can own one room.

L0326.text: Worse, a store can accept the condition and silently ignore it.
L0326.spoken: Worse, a store can accept the condition and silently ignore it.

L0327.text: So before it serves, every celld node makes four test writes: create, refuse a second create, update, refuse a stale update. Two must fail.
L0327.spoken: So before it serves, every cell D node makes four test writes: create, refuse a second create, update, refuse a stale update. Two must fail.

L0328.text: Then it checks a ranged read. No node can skip the test.
L0328.spoken: Then it checks a ranged read. No node can skip the test.

L0329.text: A bucket earns its place by refusing, on demand.
L0329.spoken: A bucket earns its place by refusing, on demand.

L0330.text: One more thing to notice. The Well referees one key at a time: one Plate for one room.
L0330.spoken: One more thing to notice. The Well referees one key at a time: one Plate for one room.

L0331.text: It makes no promise that two rooms commit as one.
L0331.spoken: It makes no promise that two rooms commit as one.

L0332.text: And if the Well goes quiet, no house can take a Plate at all.
L0332.spoken: And if the Well goes quiet, no house can take a Plate at all.

L0401.text: August, 2026. A second desk, a second lamp: the Deno team releases celld.
L0401.spoken: August, 2026. A second desk, a second lamp: the Dee-no team releases cell D.

L0402.text: Ryan Dahl, of Deno, had started it, and he later told us why.
L0402.spoken: Ryan Dahl, of Dee-no, had started it, and he later told us why.

L0403.text: He wanted a single binary, written in Rust, whose only outside service is object storage.
L0403.spoken: He wanted a single binary, written in Rust, whose only outside service is object storage.

L0404.text: celld runs a Workers application on machines you own: Durable Objects, self-hosted and distributed, with long-term state in a bucket.
L0404.spoken: cell D runs a Workers application on machines you own: Durable Objects, self-hosted and distributed, with long-term state in a bucket.

L0405.text: Its README says it needs no consensus service. By now we know where the consensus went: inside the well.
L0405.spoken: Its read-me says it needs no consensus service. By now we know where the consensus went: inside the well.

L0406.text: Its log replicator descends from a Rust reimplementation of Litestream.
L0406.spoken: Its log replicator descends from a Rust reimplementation of Lightstream.

L0407.text: In October the two would write one post together. In it, Kenton Varda, of Cloudflare, named the gap.
L0407.spoken: In October the two would write one post together. In it, Kenton Varda, of Cloudflare, named the gap.

L0408.text: workerd's Durable Objects ran as a single instance: good enough for local testing, unable to scale. He called it workerd's one big gap in production readiness.
L0408.spoken: worker D's Durable Objects ran as a single instance: good enough for local testing, unable to scale. He called it worker D's one big gap in production readiness.

L0409.text: And he wrote that when the Deno team released celld in August, “we were delighted.”
L0409.spoken: And he wrote that when the Dee-no team released cell D in August, "we were delighted."

L0410.text: Two lamps in one frame. Two ropes, beginning to braid.
L0410.spoken: Two lamps in one frame. Two ropes, beginning to braid.

L0411.text: On the ninth of October, 2026, Deno and Cloudflare announced that the whole Deno team was joining Cloudflare.
L0411.spoken: On the ninth of October, twenty twenty-six, Dee-no and Cloudflare announced that the whole Dee-no team was joining Cloudflare.

L0412.text: These are plans, as announced. The Deno runtime gets one more year of bug-fix and security releases.
L0412.spoken: These are plans, as announced. The Dee-no runtime gets one more year of bug-fix and security releases.

L0413.text: After that year, Ryan Dahl writes, the team's work on the Deno runtime comes to an end.
L0413.spoken: After that year, Ryan Dahl writes, the team's work on the Dee-no runtime comes to an end.

L0414.text: Deno Deploy runs six more months. JSR and rusty_v8 continue. Deno stays open source.
L0414.spoken: Dee-no Deploy runs six more months. J S R and rusty vee-eight continue. Dee-no stays open source.

L0415.text: Cloudflare filed its post under acquisitions, yet neither post states a price or any terms. We will not guess at them.
L0415.spoken: Cloudflare filed its post under acquisitions, yet neither post states a price or any terms. We will not guess at them.

L0416.text: Ryan Dahl and Bert Belder are to lead a first-class, supported way to run workerd yourself.
L0416.spoken: Ryan Dahl and Bert Belder are to lead a first-class, supported way to run worker D yourself.

L0418.text: On the evening of the twenty-eighth of October, Pacific time, Ryan Dahl's commit landed in workerd, calling itself a beginning.
L0418.spoken: On the evening of the twenty-eighth of October, Pacific time, Ryan Dahl's commit landed in worker D, calling itself a beginning.

L0419.text: Several processes share one bucket; each object has one owner at a time, and if an owner dies, the message says, another picks it up.
L0419.spoken: Several processes share one bucket; each object has one owner at a time, and if an owner dies, the message says, another picks it up.

L0420.text: It is experimental. For now, a write is acknowledged only once the bucket holds all of it.
L0420.spoken: It is experimental. For now, a write is acknowledged only once the bucket holds all of it.

L0421.text: And one plain line: “Alarms are not supported yet.”
L0421.spoken: And one plain line: "Alarms are not supported yet."

L0422.text: Two days later, alarms landed. The next day, facets.
L0422.spoken: Two days later, alarms landed. The next day, facets.

L0501.text: Open the Plate. In workerd's cluster it has three tiles: the house that owns the room, an epoch, and a third, called from.
L0501.spoken: Open the Plate. In worker D's cluster it has three tiles: the house that owns the room, an epoch, and a third, called from.

L0502.text: The epoch is a count that goes up with every new claim. The from tile names the last epoch that actually opened.
L0502.spoken: The epoch is a count that goes up with every new claim. The from tile names the last epoch that actually opened.

L0503.text: The code calls it the only authority on who owns the room.
L0503.spoken: The code calls it the only authority on who owns the room.

L0504.text: To claim, a keeper offers the version it read. If the Plate names a house whose lease has run out, the claim writes the next epoch, and at most one claimant wins.
L0504.spoken: To claim, a keeper offers the version it read. If the Plate names a house whose lease has run out, the claim writes the next epoch, and at most one claimant wins.

L0505.text: If that house is still alive, the request goes there instead. A brand-new room is born already open.
L0505.spoken: If that house is still alive, the request goes there instead. A brand-new room is born already open.

L0507.text: A house may serve only while it holds a lease: a candle on its sill, relit at each renewal.
L0507.spoken: A house may serve only while it holds a lease: a candle on its sill, relit at each renewal.

L0508.text: In workerd the lease is twenty seconds. A house renews every three, gives each attempt four, and retries a failure after one.
L0508.spoken: In worker D the lease is twenty seconds. A house renews every three, gives each attempt four, and retries a failure after one.

L0509.text: A clock may be two seconds off the bucket's, so the painted band at the candle's foot is twice that: four seconds.
L0509.spoken: A clock may be two seconds off the bucket's, so the painted band at the candle's foot is twice that: four seconds.

L0510.text: If this lease runs out at twenty thousand milliseconds, the house may serve only while its clock reads under sixteen thousand.
L0510.spoken: If this lease runs out at twenty thousand milliseconds, the house may serve only while its clock reads under sixteen thousand.

L0511.text: And it may start a renewal only under twelve thousand, so even a full four-second attempt ends before the band.
L0511.spoken: And it may start a renewal only under twelve thousand, so even a full four-second attempt ends before the band.

L0512.text: Lines on a ruler, not promises about timers.
L0512.spoken: Lines on a ruler, not promises about timers.

L0513.text: Why give each renewal four seconds, and not two? The code keeps a scar.
L0513.spoken: Why give each renewal four seconds, and not two? The code keeps a scar.

L0514.text: A comment records that Cloudflare's R2 stalls writes for about five and a half seconds at every five-minute mark, and that a two-second limit once stopped every node.
L0514.spoken: A comment records that Cloudflare's R two stalls writes for about five and a half seconds at every five-minute mark, and that a two-second limit once stopped every node.

L0515.text: So failed renewals are retried while the lease still holds through the attempt.
L0515.spoken: So failed renewals are retried while the lease still holds through the attempt.

L0516.text: A's keeper falls asleep: a paused process.
L0516.spoken: A's keeper falls asleep: a paused process.

L0517.text: Pull the pin, so A never checks its own candle.
L0517.spoken: Pull the pin, so A never checks its own candle.

L0518.text: The candle burns through the band. B sees that A's lease has run out, and claims the room.
L0518.spoken: The candle burns through the band. B sees that A's lease has run out, and claims the room.

L0519.text: A wakes and goes on serving. Two rooms.
L0519.spoken: A wakes and goes on serving. Two rooms.

L0520.text: Pin back. Waking, A checks its candle first. Past the band, it serves nothing, closes its own shutters, and its lamp goes out.
L0520.spoken: Pin back. Waking, A checks its candle first. Past the band, it serves nothing, closes its own shutters, and its lamp goes out.

L0521.text: A house that cannot renew in time does the same while its lease still holds: gone before anyone may take over. That is fencing.
L0521.spoken: A house that cannot renew in time does the same while its lease still holds: gone before anyone may take over. That is fencing.

L0522.text: Notice what B never knew. A timeout proves silence. It does not prove death.
L0522.spoken: Notice what B never knew. A timeout proves silence. It does not prove death.

L0523.text: Safety comes from A stopping itself, and from a second look at the Plate.
L0523.spoken: Safety comes from A stopping itself, and from a second look at the Plate.

L0524.text: One soft spot: each house measures its clock against the bucket's, and when it cannot, it assumes zero.
L0524.spoken: One soft spot: each house measures its clock against the bucket's, and when it cannot, it assumes zero.

L0525.text: So the clock is not the last line of defence; the second look is.
L0525.spoken: So the clock is not the last line of defence; the second look is.

L0526.text: celld, a different implementation, uses ten-second leases, and when the Well proves a write it does the same: it reads the record, not a clock.
L0526.spoken: cell D, a different implementation, uses ten-second leases, and when the Well proves a write it does the same: it reads the record, not a clock.

L0527.text: Claimed is not opened, and the difference decides which past the room comes back with.
L0527.spoken: Claimed is not opened, and the difference decides which past the room comes back with.

L0528.text: Made-up numbers. A opened epoch seven: A, seven, from seven. The crown is lit.
L0528.spoken: Made-up numbers. A opened epoch seven: A, seven, from seven. The crown is lit.

L0529.text: B claims: B, eight, from seven. The from tile stays at seven, and the crown is dark.
L0529.spoken: B claims: B, eight, from seven. The from tile stays at seven, and the crown is dark.

L0530.text: To open, B must restore seven's log, upload a snapshot, and then make the opening write that sets the from tile to eight.
L0530.spoken: To open, B must restore seven's log, upload a snapshot, and then make the opening write that sets the from tile to eight.

L0531.text: That flicker in House B, the night A went dark? B died first. C claims: C, nine, from seven, and recovers seven, because eight never opened and acknowledged nothing.
L0531.spoken: That flicker in House B, the night A went dark? B died first. C claims: C, nine, from seven, and recovers seven, because eight never opened and acknowledged nothing.

L0532.text: Rewind. Had B opened, the Plate would read B, eight, from eight, and C would recover eight.
L0532.spoken: Rewind. Had B opened, the Plate would read B, eight, from eight, and C would recover eight.

L0601.text: Inside the lantern, SQLite keeps the room in a file. But it does not write changes there first.
L0601.spoken: Inside the lantern, S Q L lite keeps the room in a file. But it does not write changes there first.

L0602.text: It writes them to a second file beside it: a write-ahead log. Think of it as a ribbon.
L0602.spoken: It writes them to a second file beside it: a write-ahead log. Think of it as a ribbon.

L0603.text: It starts with a leader, thirty-two bytes long. Then frames: each a twenty-four-byte tab and one page.
L0603.spoken: It starts with a leader, thirty-two bytes long. Then frames: each a twenty-four-byte tab and one page.

L0604.text: On a transaction's last frame, the tab records how many pages the database has after the commit. Other frames hold zero there.
L0604.spoken: On a transaction's last frame, the tab records how many pages the database has after the commit. Other frames hold zero there.

L0605.text: We draw it as a red stamp. That number is the commit mark.
L0605.spoken: We draw it as a red stamp. That number is the commit mark.

L0606.text: workerd's keeper hears every write to the ribbon, holds the frames since the last stamp, and cuts only when a stamped frame is complete.
L0606.spoken: worker D's keeper hears every write to the ribbon, holds the frames since the last stamp, and cuts only when a stamped frame is complete.

L0607.text: One cut, one whole transaction. Nothing half-finished ever leaves the room.
L0607.spoken: One cut, one whole transaction. Nothing half-finished ever leaves the room.

L0608.text: A transaction that rolls back leaves frames with no stamp, and the next writes straight over them.
L0608.spoken: A transaction that rolls back leaves frames with no stamp, and the next writes straight over them.

L0609.text: When SQLite copies the ribbon into its main file and starts a fresh one, the keeper starts fresh too.
L0609.spoken: When S Q L lite copies the ribbon into its main file and starts a fresh one, the keeper starts fresh too.

L0610.text: The cut lengths go down to the Well as scrolls: each page once, in its newest version.
L0610.spoken: The cut lengths go down to the Well as scrolls: each page once, in its newest version.

L0611.text: Every scroll's cord records a checksum and its length, so a damaged or short scroll refuses to be read, rather than read wrong.
L0611.spoken: Every scroll's cord records a checksum and its length, so a damaged or short scroll refuses to be read, rather than read wrong.

L0612.text: Each epoch's shelf starts with a Book, a snapshot of what it inherited; a new Book goes down before old scrolls are cleared.
L0612.spoken: Each epoch's shelf starts with a Book, a snapshot of what it inherited; a new Book goes down before old scrolls are cleared.

L0613.text: This is workerd's own format. celld writes a different one, called LTX.
L0613.spoken: This is worker D's own format. cell D writes a different one, called L T X.

L0614.text: Now the tick itself, in workerd. Message forty-two is written; its reply waits behind the latch.
L0614.spoken: Now the tick itself, in worker D. Message forty-two is written; its reply waits behind the latch.

L0615.text: The keeper cuts the transaction, and sends the scroll down to the Well.
L0615.spoken: The keeper cuts the transaction, and sends the scroll down to the Well.

L0616.text: Then, before it rings the bell, the keeper looks up at the Plate one more time. Still A. Still epoch seven.
L0616.spoken: Then, before it rings the bell, the keeper looks up at the Plate one more time. Still A. Still epoch seven.

L0617.text: Only then the bell. The latch lifts. The tick.
L0617.spoken: Only then the bell. The latch lifts. The tick.

L0619.text: Finishing inside the room is not the tick. The Well and the second look are. celld's gate holds even more: errors, and every chunk of a stream.
L0619.spoken: Finishing inside the room is not the tick. The Well and the second look are. cell D's gate holds even more: errors, and every chunk of a stream.

L0620.text: Pull the pin, and the keeper never looks up.
L0620.spoken: Pull the pin, and the keeper never looks up.

L0621.text: A sends its scroll with its lease in order, then the whole house freezes, like the sleeper. B claims epoch eight, and A's scroll lands on epoch seven's shelf.
L0621.spoken: A sends its scroll with its lease in order, then the whole house freezes, like the sleeper. B claims epoch eight, and A's scroll lands on epoch seven's shelf.

L0622.text: A rings the bell anyway: a tick for a write that B may never see.
L0622.spoken: A rings the bell anyway: a tick for a write that B may never see.

L0623.text: Pin back. A looks up: the Plate says eight. No bell; the letter becomes an error, and the old scroll is cleared later.
L0623.spoken: Pin back. A looks up: the Plate says eight. No bell; the letter becomes an error, and the old scroll is cleared later.

L0624.text: One honest limit: if a reply is lost on its way home, the sender cannot tell whether the write happened.
L0624.spoken: One honest limit: if a reply is lost on its way home, the sender cannot tell whether the write happened.

L0625.text: A missing tick does not prove a write absent. Durability is not the same as exactly once.
L0625.spoken: A missing tick does not prove a write absent. Durability is not the same as exactly once.

L0701.text: Back to workerd's town, the night A went dark. House C holds the Plate: nine, from seven.
L0701.spoken: Back to worker D's town, the night A went dark. House C holds the Plate: nine, from seven.

L0702.text: First it throws away its own copy of the room.
L0702.spoken: First it throws away its own copy of the room.

L0703.text: It reads the newest Book, then each scroll in order, skipping pages already laid down.
L0703.spoken: It reads the newest Book, then each scroll in order, skipping pages already laid down.

L0704.text: A missing scroll in the middle stops the restore cold.
L0704.spoken: A missing scroll in the middle stops the restore cold.

L0705.text: A checksum can say a scroll is damaged. Never what it said.
L0705.spoken: A checksum can say a scroll is damaged. Never what it said.

L0706.text: Pages are laid down again; no code is re-run.
L0706.spoken: Pages are laid down again; no code is re-run.

L0707.text: Message forty-two is back. Only then does C send down its own Book, and open the Plate.
L0707.spoken: Message forty-two is back. Only then does C send down its own Book, and open the Plate.

L0708.text: That is the price. In workerd's cluster, every tick waits for the Well, and a second look at the Plate.
L0708.spoken: That is the price. In worker D's cluster, every tick waits for the Well, and a second look at the Plate.

L0709.text: Our bar is illustrative: a sliver of local work, then the long walk.
L0709.spoken: Our bar is illustrative: a sliver of local work, then the long walk.

L0710.text: Cloudflare's hosted relay, back in 2024, answered that with followers.
L0710.spoken: Cloudflare's hosted relay, back in 2024, answered that with followers.

L0711.text: celld uses followers too: a neighbour's disk can answer much sooner than the Well.
L0711.spoken: cell D uses followers too: a neighbour's disk can answer much sooner than the Well.

L0713.text: This is celld's town, version 0.6.3. By default, the owner hands each write to one or two neighbours.
L0713.spoken: This is cell D's town, version zero point six point three. By default, the owner hands each write to one or two neighbours.

L0714.text: Each must press the page onto its own disk before it answers. That press is called fsync.
L0714.spoken: Each must press the page onto its own disk before it answers. That press is called F sync.

L0715.text: When every neighbour in the proof has pressed, the bell can ring before the page reaches the Well. The upload follows.
L0715.spoken: When every neighbour in the proof has pressed, the bell can ring before the page reaches the Well. The upload follows.

L0716.text: Now count. The owner never counts itself.
L0716.spoken: Now count. The owner never counts itself.

L0717.text: One house alone gets no fleet. It falls back on the Well's proof: much slower, still correct.
L0717.spoken: One house alone gets no fleet. It falls back on the Well's proof: much slower, still correct.

L0718.text: Two running houses: one neighbour, enough for a proof. Three or more: two neighbours, three copies.
L0718.spoken: Two running houses: one neighbour, enough for a proof. Three or more: two neighbours, three copies.

L0719.text: Until a second neighbour joins, a fresh write's proof rests on two copies: the owner's and one neighbour's.
L0719.spoken: Until a second neighbour joins, a fresh write's proof rests on two copies: the owner's and one neighbour's.

L0720.text: Now replay that night in celld's town: the owner dies while forty-two lives only in the neighbours' notebooks.
L0720.spoken: Now replay that night in cell D's town: the owner dies while forty-two lives only in the neighbours' notebooks.

L0722.text: In celld's Well, each epoch writes under its own shelf, so a stale owner can only add to an old shelf, never to the new owner's.
L0722.spoken: In cell D's Well, each epoch writes under its own shelf, so a stale owner can only add to an old shelf, never to the new owner's.

L0723.text: That fences the Well. It cannot fetch what only the neighbours hold. Forty-two is gone.
L0723.spoken: That fences the Well. It cannot fetch what only the neighbours hold. Forty-two is gone.

L0724.text: Or the old owner was only asleep, and wakes to ring one more bell.
L0724.spoken: Or the old owner was only asleep, and wakes to ring one more bell.

L0725.text: Pin back. Before its first tick from the neighbours, each celld session creates its own log record in the Well.
L0725.spoken: Pin back. Before its first tick from the neighbours, each cell D session creates its own log record in the Well.

L0726.text: So a successor reads that record before it reads the Well.
L0726.spoken: So a successor reads that record before it reads the Well.

L0727.text: Absent: the old session never ticked ahead of the Well. Sealed: someone already recovered it.
L0727.spoken: Absent: the old session never ticked ahead of the Well. Sealed: someone already recovered it.

L0728.text: Open, or still recovering: fence it with a compare and swap. Seal every neighbour it can reach, collect their pages, upload them, and mark the record sealed.
L0728.spoken: Open, or still recovering: fence it with a compare and swap. Seal every neighbour it can reach, collect their pages, upload them, and mark the record sealed.

L0729.text: Only then restore. With its neighbours sealed, the old owner cannot win another bell.
L0729.spoken: Only then restore. With its neighbours sealed, the old owner cannot win another bell.

L0730.text: Now the hard rule. At least one current neighbour must hand over its complete range of retained pages.
L0730.spoken: Now the hard rule. At least one current neighbour must hand over its complete range of retained pages.

L0731.text: Two made-up cases. One notebook is water-damaged, but the other is complete: recovery proceeds.
L0731.spoken: Two made-up cases. One notebook is water-damaged, but the other is complete: recovery proceeds.

L0732.text: Now one notebook is incomplete, and the other damaged. Nobody can prove the whole tail, so the door stays shut.
L0732.spoken: Now one notebook is incomplete, and the other damaged. Nobody can prove the whole tail, so the door stays shut.

L0733.text: And a neighbour that answers with an error has not proved its pages absent.
L0733.spoken: And a neighbour that answers with an error has not proved its pages absent.

L0734.text: The room would rather stay shut than come back missing a promise.
L0734.spoken: The room would rather stay shut than come back missing a promise.

L0735.text: Houses that restart together still lend each other their notebooks. Recovery can take minutes; a waiting request gives up only after two hundred and forty tries.
L0735.spoken: Houses that restart together still lend each other their notebooks. Recovery can take minutes; a waiting request gives up only after two hundred and forty tries.

L0736.text: In our harbour the notebooks are whole. The lantern relights; forty-two keeps its tick.
L0736.spoken: In our harbour the notebooks are whole. The lantern relights; forty-two keeps its tick.

L0801.text: Four pins, in the order we pulled them: the Tooth, the band on the candle, the second look, the neighbours' seal.
L0801.spoken: Four pins, in the order we pulled them: the Tooth, the band on the candle, the second look, the neighbours' seal.

L0802.text: Pull any one, and a promise breaks.
L0802.spoken: Pull any one, and a promise breaks.

L0803.text: So what travels, when a room travels, is not the bucket alone.
L0803.spoken: So what travels, when a room travels, is not the bucket alone.

L0804.text: It is the bucket's refusals on one key, and its fresh reads; leases, with clocks kept close; and, as celld asks, a supervisor to restart a house that fenced itself.
L0804.spoken: It is the bucket's refusals on one key, and its fresh reads; leases, with clocks kept close; and, as cell D asks, a supervisor to restart a house that fenced itself.

L0805.text: And a runtime that cuts the ribbon, uploads and looks again; in celld's fleet, one that also seals and collects before it replays.
L0805.spoken: And a runtime that cuts the ribbon, uploads and looks again; in cell D's fleet, one that also seals and collects before it replays.

L0806.text: The small print, as of the thirty-first of October, 2026.
L0806.spoken: The small print, as of the thirty-first of October, twenty twenty-six.

L0807.text: workerd's clustering is three days old, and still experimental.
L0807.spoken: worker D's clustering is three days old, and still experimental.

L0808.text: Its tests check one writer, forwarding, and takeover after a kill. We read them. We did not run them.
L0808.spoken: Its tests check one writer, forwarding, and takeover after a kill. We read them. We did not run them.

L0809.text: The alarm tests check the cases they stage. They do not establish exactly-once effects for every application.
L0809.spoken: The alarm tests check the cases they stage. They do not establish exactly-once effects for every application.

L0810.text: celld documents its own limits, and wants bucket lifecycle rules that leave its records alone.
L0810.spoken: cell D documents its own limits, and wants bucket lifecycle rules that leave its records alone.

L0811.text: And workerd, on its own, is not a sandbox for untrusted code.
L0811.spoken: And worker D, on its own, is not a sandbox for untrusted code.

L0812.text: The two lamps, once more. The announced plan stands, and the commit called itself a beginning.
L0812.spoken: The two lamps, once more. The announced plan stands, and the commit called itself a beginning.

L0813.text: celld's code and ideas are to be merged into workerd, and Ryan Dahl writes that the team's future work goes into this shared platform.
L0813.spoken: cell D's code and ideas are to be merged into worker D, and Ryan Dahl writes that the team's future work goes into this shared platform.

L0814.text: And the Well? It does not run your code, make two rooms commit as one, promise exactly once, or keep the town open when it goes quiet.
L0814.spoken: And the Well? It does not run your code, make two rooms commit as one, promise exactly once, or keep the town open when it goes quiet.

L0815.text: Dawn over the harbour. The lantern burns in House C, and the sender's slip still carries its tick.
L0815.spoken: Dawn over the harbour. The lantern burns in House C, and the sender's slip still carries its tick.

L0816.text: A tick is not a feeling. It is a proof.
L0816.spoken: A tick is not a feeling. It is a proof.

L0817.text: The bytes were in the Well, and the Plate still named its owner when the bell rang.
L0817.spoken: The bytes were in the Well, and the Plate still named its owner when the bell rang.

L0818.text: The harbour was made up. The code is real.
L0818.spoken: The harbour was made up. The code is real.

PROLOGUE AND TITLE, in D. The motif family is born here (score/motifs.md). (1) ch01-s01: the harbour drone and an open D-A string fifth; a small harp figure (D, A, E) as the lantern resolves, in the hold before L0101; one soft harp A in the breath after 'forty-two'; the strings fall away on 'door' (the room holds its breath). T, the tick, is born: the piano A in the colon breath after 'tick', the D after 'saved', ringing into the hold. (2) ch01-s02: NO MUSIC for the failure. Everything cuts with A's lamp on the gutter beat; only a low wind under L0105. One low string D returns as House C lights; the bundle climbs on a slow harp A2 to D3 (the tick's fourth, low); after 'true' T answers itself, warmer (piano doubled by harp an octave down). (3) ch01-s03: the drone returns under the crane; Dm9 in the breath after 'promises', Bbmaj7 on 'nothing', C(add9) under the newer promise with one harp E on 'move'; Gm/Bb under the question, cut short at the end of 'portable' so the question hangs in the air. (4) ch01-s04: P whole for the first time on the piano (A D, E F, G, F E, D), the tick as its head, over Dm, Bbmaj7, C and a final D-A-E (no third: the F-sharp is withheld until dawn). The final D is struck in the breath before L0117 and rings to the join; nothing new sounds after it.

THE COMMIT, THE PLATE AND THE CANDLE. (1) ch04-s04: alone in the hold the braid resolves into one held F chord (piano F and C meeting the cello's F); a low pad under the commit (F, B-flat, C, Dm, one per line); a two-note harp step after 'landed' and a step higher after 'facets' (the calendar); on 'Let us open it' the chord opens upward to A-sus and the terrace drone enters. (2) ch05-s01: the terrace drone; three pizzicato tocks after 'tiles'; a count up after 'claim'; the Tooth's dry click after L0504 ('at most one claimant wins'); a light pizzicato run after 'instead' (the chalk arrow); T after 'born already open'. (3) ch05-s02: the lease clock C (pizzicato A-D, one per second) from 'candle'; one soft harp pluck after each number in the timetable ('twenty', 'three', 'four', 'one'); the band arrives on a darker chord (G minor over B-flat) on 'band'; the two ruled lines: an A octave on 'sixteen', a D fitting inside it on 'twelve'. (4) ch05-s03: bowed air (low band-passed noise) swells from the 'stall' beat; SILENCE when every lamp gutters on the 'snuff' beat; a reversed string swell into the 'retry' beat. (5) ch05-s04: a harp lullaby for the sleeping keeper, the clock slowed to one tock every two seconds; pad and clock cut on 'Pull'; the lullaby sours (A-flat for A) on the 'burn' beat; two clashing drones (strings D against cello E-flat) on 'Two rooms', out after 'Pin back'; a soft wooden knock after 'shutters', then silence; the maxim over a single low D from 'timeout'. (6) ch05-s05: two pizzicato clocks out of phase drift together and one drops out on the 'zero' beat (the snapped thread); celld's terrace in G (harp G-D-B and a G pad, the clock motif on D-G). (7) ch05-s06: D minor; one pizzicato clockwork step per printed stamp; T small after 'The crown is lit'; S (A-sus4) held while B's crown stays dark, the piano A withheld above it; SILENCE on 'died'; a resolving cello line A to D on 'recovers'; a reversed swell into 'Rewind'; a quiet two-chord close: Bbmaj7 after 'Rewind', then D-A-D in the breath after 'read B' (the last strike), before 'eight'.

THE RIBBON. (1) ch06-s01: alone in the hold, an open A-E pad and a piano A-E; a pizzicato ribbon figure after 'log'; a light tick per frame after 'frames'; the red stamp is a low, warm thud (piano and harp A1) in the breath after 'stamp'; a quiet A minor (add9) from 'That' under 'commit mark'. (2) ch06-s02: a light pulse of frames from 'hears' under L0606; a crisp pizzicato snip after L0606 and after 'transaction', in the clear; a muffled paste-over on 'over'; a soft E to A cadence after 'starts fresh too'. (3) ch06-s03: D minor; W in the cello as the scrolls go down; a muted refusal knock (B-flat over A) after 'read wrong'; the Book: a low harp thud after 'Book'; celld's shelf a brief G colour from 'celld' to the end of L0613. (4) ch06-s04, the tick built in full: the reply waits (piano A after 'latch'); W quickly down for the scroll under L0615; a held breath (the pad thins to one A) on 'looks'; two soft harp glints after 'Still A' and 'Still epoch seven'; the bell (low harp and piano D-A) after 'bell'; the latch lifts (A) after 'lifts'; T complete (D over D-A-D strings) after 'The tick': the first full tick since the prologue. A lighter counting figure after 'are'. (5) ch06-s05: SILENCE from L0620 (the pin); a frozen held A from 'freezes'; the false bell (D against E-flat) after 'bell' and T broken (A then E-flat) after 'anyway'; no bell for the true check, only a low knock after 'error'; the coda: a B-flat pad from L0624 and the piano A alone after 'absent' (the last strike), unresolved: durability is not exactly once.

THE NEIGHBOURS. (1) ch07-s01: alone in the hold, the harbour drone under the iris and a D minor pad; a soft page-turn pulse (pizzicato D-A) from 'scroll', stopped dead on 'cold', resuming for L0706; T on 'back' (A on the word, D in the breath after it). (2) ch07-s02: the drone thins; W at half speed in the cello from 'waits' (the long walk); a cool A minor (add9) after 'followers'; on 'Change the lamps' everything falls away. (3) ch07-s03: celld's town in G, the harp alone in the gap before L0713; a dry low knock on each 'press' and on 'pressed'; T on 'ring', before any well sound; a faint low harp D on 'upload'. (4) ch07-s03b: W slow in the cello after 'fleet' for the lone house, then the bell after 'still correct'; a knock on 'Two' and on 'Three'; the three-copies chord, the fullest moment so far, struck by the harp in the gap after L0718 over a lighter string chord; thinned to two notes on 'two' in L0719. (5) ch07-s04: SILENCE for the failure from 'dies'; one hollow knock after 'Pull the pin'; a low held D under the shelves, gone before 'Forty-two'; the stale bell (D against E-flat) after 'bell' and T broken after L0724; the green pad creeps back after 'Pin back'. (6) ch07-s05: the parchment hush (the pad very low); a dry click on 'fence'; a soft thud on 'Seal' and on 'reach'; a low harp D on 'upload'; the gate opens on a held piano A after 'restore', unresolved. (7) ch07-s06: case one resolves on a warm open fifth on 'proceeds'; a reversed breath into case two; S (A-sus4) from 'damaged', never resolving; T withheld; a single low muffled bell after L0734: a door that did not open. (8) ch07-s07: a patient pizzicato loop for the retries over S; S resolves to the open fifth D-A on 'relights'; T full and clear: A in the breath after 'whole', D in the breath after 'relights' (the last strike), ringing under 'forty-two keeps its tick', held warm into the iris.

WHAT TRAVELS, and dawn. (1) ch08-s01: alone in the hold, a low D minor pad. The four pins, one gesture each in the breaths of L0801: the Tooth's dry click after 'Tooth', the candle's clock (A-D) after 'candle', the second look's bell (harp D-A) after 'look', the seal's soft low thud after L0801. One shared sting (D, E-flat, A) on 'Pull'; then a slow, steady clock ostinato (A-D) under L0803 to L0805, the harmony walking Dm, B-flat, C, Dm. (2) ch08-s02: the ostinato drops to a clerk's metronome (one A every two seconds); one soft harp A after L0806 (the thirty-first: alarms, no chime); the G colour under L0810 (celld). (3) ch08-s03: the two lamps in ONE voice on the piano: P's rising head (A D E F) in the gap before L0812 and R's falling tail (E after 'more', D after 'stands', A after L0812); a single held D under L0814 as the camera finds the paper Well; a soft muted pluck after 'code', 'one', 'once' and 'quiet', each quieter, the last barely there. (4) ch08-s04, DAWN: in the gap after L0814 the drone opens into D major (strings D-F#-A: the first F-sharp of the film) and the harp sings P's head in D major (A D E F#); T slow on 'proof' (A after 'feeling', D after 'proof', harmonised in D major for the first time); the bell after L0817 ('rang'); the last chord, D major with an added ninth (piano, harp, low strings), strikes after 'The code is real' (the last strike) and rings in clear air under the end card into the final fade.
